title: Money from recording and lending at interest
summary: Ory demanded double scale, lent money at 10% and left Chicago well off.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I asked Ed one question. Why he didn't have a band of his own in Chicago. Yeah. You know the answer I got? He was fed up with the responsibilities. Yeah.

And on every recording date, since he had to record starting at 8.30 in the morning, he told him he was too tired. He just finished at 4.30. He always ran his price up. He got double what the leader got on every recording session. And he finally got to the point where he was making so dog-gone much money that everyone who was spending theirs right, left and forward and he was being nice and saving with his. He would lend it to them at 10% interest mind you. Is that so? And he left Chicago well padded. The business on the side, no?

Yeah. Yeah, the last band I played was a guy who wanted to kill me because I hadn't loaned him $500. He was married and he... Counting some girl in trouble. Some young girl, you know. He wanted to shoot me because I wouldn't loan him $500. I said, on what? Why are you security? What have you got? He said, I got the cost. I wouldn't give you $2 for it myself. I said, can you get any money out of the bank, from the bank? I said, loan on that cost. He said, no. I said, why pick on a poor man like me?

He even got more money than Louie did on the recordings. For the good and simple reason, he got to the point where he was just too tired. Unless he was paid enough, he didn't want to pick up his heart and blow.
